title: Guard: respect non-compactness of B^(H) (no termwise SV product)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Conceptual consistency / definitional-drift guard.** The problem statement asserts $B^{(H)}$ is bounded but **non-compact**. Indeed $(B^{(H)})(B^{(H)})^*=\mathcal H$, the Hilbert matrix $\mathcal H_{ij}=1/(i+j-1)$, which has $\|\mathcal H\|=\pi$ and purely continuous spectrum $[0,\pi]$ with no eigenvalues (Magnus/Rosenblum); hence the singular values of $B^{(H)}$ do NOT tend to $0$.

Any proof step that implicitly treats $B^{(H)}$ as compact — e.g. multiplying singular-value sequences of $B^{(H)}$ and $J$ termwise, or asserting $\sigma_i(A)=\sigma_i(B^{(H)})\sigma_i(J)$ — is INVALID. The smoothing in $A$ comes entirely from $J$ (whose smooth range consists of analytic functions $(1-t^i)/i$), and the correct conclusion (severe ill-posedness) arises precisely because the moment operator amplifies these analytic functions. Verify every step respects non-compactness of $B^{(H)}$.

**Difficulty:** conceptual; it is a trap that must be avoided rather than an estimate to prove, but is a genuine logical requirement of any correct argument.
